title: Restriction surjects on inertia in a Galois tower
statement:
Let $A$ be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ a tower such that $L/K$ and $M/K$ are Galois: algebraic, separable, and normal (every minimal polynomial of an element splits over the extension field) [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The extensions need not be finite. Let $B\subseteq L$ and $C\subseteq M$ be the integral closures of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Choose a prime $\mathfrak r\subset C$ and set $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak r\cap B$. The groups act on the integral closures by restriction. Define
$$I_{\mathfrak r}=\{g\in\operatorname{Gal}(M/K):g\mathfrak r=\mathfrak r,\ g|_{\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak r)}=1\},\quad I_{\mathfrak q}=\{h\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K):h\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q,\ h|_{\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)}=1\}.$$
Then restriction induces a surjective homomorphism $I_{\mathfrak r}\to I_{\mathfrak q}$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-algebraic-extension-normal] to $A\subset L$ and $A\subset M$. Thus $B,C$ are normal domains with fraction fields $L,M$, and $C$ is integrally closed in $M$. Moreover $C$ is exactly the integral closure of $B$ in $M$: if $x\in C$, its monic equation over $A$ is also one over $B$; conversely, a monic equation over $B\subset C$ makes $x\in M$ integral over $C$, hence $x\in C$. The inclusion $B/\mathfrak q\hookrightarrow C/\mathfrak r$ is injective by the definition of contraction. Consequently it extends by $a/b\mapsto a/b$ to an inclusion $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak r)$, where $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak r)=\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak r)$.

source.place: Tag 0BSX, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois-compare, proof; expanding the last sentence using Tag 0BRK (1),(2).

proof.text: Restriction to $L$ is defined for every $g\in\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)$: normality of $L/K$ implies that $g(x)\in L$ for $x\in L$, since $g(x)$ is another root of the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $K$; applying this also to $g^{-1}$ gives equality of the image with $L$. Applying $g$ to monic equations over $A$ shows $g(C)=C$ and $g(B)=B$. If $g\in I_{\mathfrak r}$, then $g(\mathfrak q)=g(\mathfrak r)\cap g(B)=\mathfrak q$, and the residue action of $g|_L$ on $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is the restriction of the identity action on $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$. Therefore $g|_L\in I_{\mathfrak q}$. Restriction commutes with composition and identity, so it defines the asserted homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BSX, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois-compare, proof; expanding the last sentence using Tag 0BRK (1),(2).

proof.text: Fix $h\in I_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-subextension-automorphism-extends], normality of $M/K$ and $L/K$ gives $\tau\in\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)$ with $\tau|_L=h$. By [lem-dl-a1-galois-over-intermediate], $M/L$ is Galois even when either extension is infinite. Step 1 supplies precisely the normal base domain $B$, its fraction field $L$, and its integral closure $C$ in $M$ needed to apply [lem-dl-a1-galois-prime-residue-lifting] over $B$.

source.place: Tag 0BSX, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois-compare, proof; expanding the last sentence using Tag 0BRK (1),(2).

proof.text: The primes $\tau(\mathfrak r)$ and $\mathfrak r$ of $C$ contract to the same prime of $B$, because $\tau(\mathfrak r)\cap B=h(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q$. Apply part (1) of [lem-dl-a1-galois-prime-residue-lifting] with base $B$, fraction field $L$, extension $M/L$, and these two primes. Obtain $\rho\in\operatorname{Gal}(M/L)$ satisfying $\rho\tau(\mathfrak r)=\mathfrak r$. Put $d=\rho\tau$. Then $d$ stabilizes $\mathfrak r$ and $d|_L=h$, since $\rho$ fixes $L$ pointwise.

source.place: Tag 0BSX, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois-compare, proof; expanding the last sentence using Tag 0BRK (1),(2).

proof.text: Let $\bar d$ be the automorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ induced by $d$. For $a,b\in B$ with $b\notin\mathfrak q$, its value on the image of $\bar a/\bar b$ is $\overline{h(a)}/\overline{h(b)}=\bar a/\bar b$, since $h\in I_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus $\bar d$ fixes $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Apply part (2) of [lem-dl-a1-galois-prime-residue-lifting], again for $B\subset C$ and $M/L$, to this automorphism. It gives $\epsilon\in\operatorname{Gal}(M/L)$ stabilizing $\mathfrak r$ whose action on $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ equals $\bar d$. This does not require the residue extension to be separable or finite.

source.place: Tag 0BSX, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois-compare, proof; expanding the last sentence using Tag 0BRK (1),(2).

proof.text: Set $g=\epsilon^{-1}d$. Both factors stabilize $\mathfrak r$, and its residue action is $\bar\epsilon^{-1}\bar d=\bar d^{-1}\bar d=1$. Hence $g\in I_{\mathfrak r}$. Because $\epsilon|_L=1$, its restriction is $g|_L=h$. Every $h\in I_{\mathfrak q}$ therefore has a preimage, proving surjectivity.
